notes: FLSA has no daily overtime, meal-break, rest-break, minimum-rest-between-shifts, predictive-scheduling, or reporting-time-pay requirement for adults.
FLSA sets no hours or time-of-day limits for 16- and 17-year-olds in non-agricultural work; only hazardous-occupation orders apply to them.
minor_limits school_week=true: 'max_hours_day' is for days school is in session; 'max_hours_non_school_day' (extra key) is the cap on a non-school day within a school week (29 CFR 570.35(a)(1),(3)).

Tipped minimum wage: max_tip_credit_per_hour 5.12 = $7.25 federal minimum wage − $2.13 cash wage (29 CFR 531.50(a)(2)); tip credit only for employees who customarily receive more than $30/month in tips and only after notice to the employee.

rules.summary: Non-exempt employees get 1.5x their regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek.

citation.title: 29 U.S.C. § 207(a)(1) — Maximum hours
citation.excerpt: for a workweek longer than forty hours ... at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate

rules.summary: The federal minimum wage is $7.25 an hour.

citation.title: 29 U.S.C. § 206(a)(1)(C) — Minimum wage
citation.excerpt: $7.25 an hour, beginning 24 months after that 60th day (i.e. July 24, 2009)

rules.summary: In a school week, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 3 hours on a school day (8 on a non-school day), 18 hours total, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.35(a) — Hours of work for minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: Not more than 3 hours in any 1 day when school is in session ... Not more than 18 hours in any 1 week when school is in session

rules.summary: When school is not in session, 14- and 15-year-olds may work up to 8 hours a day and 40 a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (9 p.m. from June 1 through Labor Day).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.35(a) — Hours of work for minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: Between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. ... except during the summer (June 1 through Labor Day) when the evening hour will be 9 p.m.

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not operate or ride on forklifts and other high-lift trucks (Hazardous Occupations Order No. 7).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.58 — Power-driven hoisting apparatus (HO 7)
citation.excerpt: operating, tending, riding upon ... high-lift truck ... highlift trucks known under such names as fork lifts, fork trucks, fork lift trucks

rules.summary: Under the FLSA an employer may pay tipped employees a cash wage of $2.13 an hour and count up to $5.12 of tips toward the $7.25 minimum wage.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 531.50 — Statutory provisions with respect to tipped employees (FLSA § 3(m)(2)(A))
citation.excerpt: The cash wage paid such employee which ... shall not be less than the cash wage required to be paid such an employee on August 20, 1996 [ i.e., $2.13]
